summary.text: Morgan McGarvey is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2022, and won re-election on November 3, 2026.

A Louisville attorney, he served in the Kentucky State Senate from 2012 to 2023, including as Senate Democratic Caucus minority leader. According to his official site, he emphasizes public education, organized labor, reproductive rights and working families.

paragraphs.text: McGarvey was born in Louisville in 1979, according to Ballotpedia; his official biography calls him a lifelong Louisvillian who graduated from Manual High School.
He earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from the University of Missouri in 2002 and a law degree from the University of Kentucky in 2007.
He worked as an attorney with Morgan & Pottinger PSC, according to Ballotpedia, and has been affiliated with the Young Professionals Association of Louisville and the New Leaders Council.
McGarvey represented District 19 in the Kentucky State Senate from 2012 to 2023, including four years as Minority Leader of the Senate Democratic Caucus.

His official biography says he wrote and passed 18 bills into law during roughly ten years in the State Senate, including an insurance mandate for low-birthweight infants and a law letting Simmons College of Kentucky lower tuition.

McGarvey was elected to the U.S. House in 2022. According to his official site, he serves on the Veterans' Affairs, Small Business and Budget committees and co-chairs the Bourbon Caucus and the Ohio River Basin Caucus.
The site says he was the first freshman Democrat to pass a bill out of the House, a bill on veterans' educational benefits.
According to his official biography, he lives in the Highlands neighborhood of Louisville with his wife, Chris, and their three children.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 70.3% of the vote to Maria Rodriguez's 29.7%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
